issues.description: Element: Animal constructor. In the problem statement UML (problem_statement.md) Animal is declared with a two-parameter constructor Animal(String, int). In the solution code (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java) the constructor is declared as public Animal(String name) (single String parameter). The template's example usage in Main.java (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java) also uses single-argument constructors for concrete animals (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle")). This inconsistency leaves students uncertain whether to implement Animal and the concrete animal constructors with one or two parameters and may cause them to implement the wrong signature relative to tests or the provided code examples.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signature consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) Update the problem statement UML to specify a single-parameter constructor Animal(String) and remove the age parameter/attribute from the UML and tasks (recommended if age is not needed for the learning objectives), or (B) Update the template and solution to add an int age field and change all animal constructors and their usages (Seal, Pig, Goat and any examples in Main) to accept (String name, int age), and add the corresponding getter/setter for age. Apply the chosen change uniformly to problem_statement.md, the template code, and the solution code.

issues.description: Element: Animal.age attribute. In the problem statement UML (problem_statement.md) Animal declares an attribute age: int. In the solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java) there is no age field; only a private String name is present. This discrepancy between the specified class attributes and the code can mislead students about required fields and whether they must implement age-related getters/setters or constructor parameters.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the attribute specification with the code. Either: (A) Remove the age attribute from the UML/problem statement and any related tasks if age is not required for learning outcomes (preferred if exercise focuses on inheritance/interfaces), or (B) Add a private int age field to the template and solution Animal class, include getter and setter methods, and add age as a constructor parameter (propagating constructor changes to concrete animals and example usages). Ensure problem_statement.md and all code examples are updated consistently.
